risks.note: The global economy is disrupted by the outbreak of war in the Middle East, with rising commodity prices, firmer inflation expectations and tighter financial conditions. Elevated energy and other commodity prices coupled with supply shock due to disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz would act as a drag on domestic production in FY 2026-27, and West Asia tensions may disrupt energy supplies and fertiliser availability - both critical inputs for agricultural production.
risks.risk: Geopolitical conflict in the Middle East and energy/commodity supply shock

risks.note: IMD's first-stage forecast puts monsoon rainfall at 92% of the Long Period Average (+/-5%), a likely below-normal outcome due to El Nino. With 51% of cultivated land rain-fed (about 40% of production) and nearly 47% of the population dependent on agriculture, a weaker monsoon could dampen rural consumption and push up food inflation - directly relevant to the group's animal nutrition, crop care, oil palm and dairy exposures.
risks.risk: Below-normal monsoon and climate variability hitting the agri value chain

risks.note: Heightened volatility in global financial markets with its spillover on domestic financial conditions would weigh on growth prospects; risks to the global outlook are described as decisively on the downside, with high public debt and eroded policy buffers adding vulnerability.
risks.risk: Global financial market volatility spilling into domestic financial conditions

risks.note: Fragmented landholdings, climate pressures, irrigation constraints and rural-to-urban migration persist as structural challenges, and land fragmentation plus income uncertainty keep farm incomes volatile - a demand risk for the agri-input and allied businesses.

The World Economic Outlook projects global growth at 3.1% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027, below recent outcomes and well under pre-pandemic averages; net external demand for India remained soft, with a prolonged conflict, deeper geopolitical fragmentation or renewed trade tensions cited as downside triggers.
risks.risk: Soft external demand and slower global growth

risks.note: The Board-framed Risk Management Policy identifies and assesses operational, strategic, financial, security, property, regulatory, reputational, cyber security and other risks, with a risk management infrastructure maintained to address them.
risks.risk: Enterprise risk spectrum covered by the Board's Risk Management Policy

risks.note: The Board acknowledges that IFC are not static and will evolve as the business, technology and even the fraud environment change in response to competition, industry practices, legislation, regulation and economic conditions, so gaps may arise; a process is in place to continuously identify such gaps and implement improved controls.
risks.risk: Evolving gaps in Internal Financial Controls as the business changes

risks.note: The regulatory environment remains focused on financial stability, transparency and consumer protection; while evolving regulations reinforce systemic resilience, they necessitate higher compliance and governance standards for the group's growing lending and wealth/asset management platform.
risks.risk: Rising regulatory and compliance burden in financial services
